Metadata.title: Trading Academy
Metadata.description: A free academy for learning crypto trading — from your first candlestick chart to advanced strategies.

Footer.disclaimer: Educational content only – not financial advice.

hero.title: Learn crypto trading — from your first candle to your own strategy
hero.description: A free, structured academy for complete beginners and experienced traders. No hype, no promises of quick profit.

why.title: Why Trading Academy
why.description: Everything you need to understand crypto markets — and nothing you don't.

free.title: Free for everyone
free.description: All courses are free. No paywall, no upsell, no hidden premium tier.

structured.title: A clear learning path
structured.description: Courses build on each other: course → module → lesson, so you always know what comes next.

levels.title: Beginner to advanced
levels.description: Start from zero or jump in at your level — every course is marked Beginner, Intermediate or Advanced.

risk.title: Risk comes first
risk.description: Losing money is part of trading. We teach risk management from the very first lesson.

levels.title: Pick your level
levels.description: Every course has a level, so you can find the right starting point.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.description: You know the basics and want to trade with a plan.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: You trade and want to sharpen your edge.

curriculum.title: The first course: Crypto basics
curriculum.description: A gentle start for complete beginners — the first course we are preparing.
modules: What is a blockchain and a cryptocurrency
Bitcoin, Ethereum and how they differ
Keeping your account and funds safe
What trading is — and its risks

free.question: Is it really free?
free.answer: Yes. All courses are free and will stay free. You won't need to pay or subscribe to learn.

advice.question: Is this financial advice?
advice.answer: No. Trading Academy is educational content only. We explain how markets work and how to manage risk — we never tell you what to buy or sell.

when.question: When will the courses be available?
when.answer: We are preparing the first course, Crypto basics, right now. It will appear here as soon as it is ready.

money.question: Do I need money to start learning?
money.answer: No. You can learn everything without risking any money. When you do decide to trade, only use money you can afford to lose.

languages.question: Which languages are available?
languages.answer: English and Czech. You can switch the language at any time in the header.

chart.illustrative: Illustrative data, not a real market

doji.name: Doji
doji.description: Open and close are almost the same – buyers and sellers are in balance and the market hesitates.

hammer.name: Hammer
hammer.description: After a fall, sellers pushed the price down, but buyers pushed it back up – a possible turn upwards.

shootingStar.name: Shooting star
shootingStar.description: After a rise, buyers pushed the price up, but sellers pushed it back down – a possible turn downwards.

bullishEngulfing.name: Bullish engulfing
bullishEngulfing.description: A green body completely covers the previous red one – buyers are taking over.

bearishEngulfing.name: Bearish engulfing
bearishEngulfing.description: A red body completely covers the previous green one – sellers are taking over.

morningStar.name: Morning star
morningStar.description: A big red candle, a small hesitant one and a big green one – a turn from a fall to a rise.

eveningStar.name: Evening star
eveningStar.description: A big green candle, a small hesitant one and a big red one – a turn from a rise to a fall.

anatomy.label: Parts of a candlestick: a rising and a falling candle. The body is between the open and close price, the wicks reach the highest and the lowest price.

blockchain.caption: Every block stores the fingerprint (hash) of the previous one. Changing an old block would change its hash and break every block after it.

sign.title: Sign
sign.text: The sender signs the payment with their private key in the wallet.

broadcast.title: Broadcast
broadcast.text: The wallet sends the transaction to the network, computers pass it on to each other.

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.text: Miners or validators check it and write it into a new block.

receive.title: Receive
receive.text: The receiver sees the coins once the block is added – more blocks on top mean more certainty.

transaction.caption: No bank sits in the middle – the network itself checks and records every payment.

privateKey.title: Private key
privateKey.text: The secret that controls your coins. Never share it with anyone.

publicKey.title: Public key
publicKey.text: Calculated from the private key. Proves your signature.

address.title: Address
address.text: Short form of the public key. Share it to receive payments.

wallet.caption: Each step works only forward: from an address nobody can find your private key.

orderBook.label: Illustrative BTC/USDT order book
orderBook.caption: Sellers wait above the price, buyers below it. The bars show how much is waiting at each price. Illustrative data.

sharedLedger.caption: Four notebooks agree, one does not. The village trusts the majority – George's twenty chickens stay a dream.

midnightEdit.label: Cartoon: at night, George secretly writes 20 chickens into his notebook by candlelight, while a chicken at the window stares in disbelief.
midnightEdit.caption: George quietly "improves" his notebook at night. The chickens have their doubts.

copyMachine.label: Cartoon: a cheerful person presses the button of a copy machine that spits out banknotes.
copyMachine.caption: If money could be copied like a file, everyone would be a millionaire. At least until lunch.

miningRace.label: Cartoon: three sweating computers race to guess a number while an electricity meter spins wildly.
miningRace.caption: Mining in a nutshell: millions of guesses per second – and an electricity meter that never rests.

pizzaDay.label: Cartoon: a happy person with two pepperoni pizzas and a price tag of 10,000 BTC.
pizzaDay.caption: 22 May 2010: two pizzas for 10,000 bitcoins, then about 41 dollars. Probably the most expensive dinner in history.

vendingMachine.label: Cartoon: a surprised customer at a vending machine labelled 'if coin → snack' that hands out a snack without any shop assistant.
vendingMachine.caption: Smart contract in a nutshell: the rules are written in code and run on their own – nobody can bend them. Not even when you ask nicely.

memeSlot.label: Cartoon: a Shiba Inu pulls the lever of a slot machine labelled MEMECOIN; the reels show ×100, ×100 and −99%.
memeSlot.caption: Memecoins in a nutshell: two reels promise a hundredfold, the third one is usually right.

feeBus.label: Cartoon: a full bus leaving in 10 minutes; a passenger waving banknotes gets on, a person with one coin waits at the stop.
feeBus.caption: Fees as a bus ride: whoever offers more gets a seat first. The rest wait for the next bus.
